blocks.text: Have you ever wondered why the value of a car decreases over time? This is due to depreciation, a key concept in accounting.

blocks.markdown: Depreciation is the process of allocating the cost of a non-current asset over its useful life. This is important because it helps businesses match the cost of an asset with the revenue it generates, adhering to the matching principle in accounting.

blocks.title: Definition of Depreciation
blocks.text: Depreciation is the systematic allocation of the cost of a tangible asset over its useful life.

blocks.markdown: There are two main methods of calculating depreciation: the straight-line method and the reducing-balance method. Each method has its own formula and application.

items: Straight-Line Method: Allocates an equal amount of depreciation each year.
Reducing-Balance Method: Allocates a decreasing amount of depreciation each year.

blocks.title: Calculating Depreciation
blocks.prompt: Calculate the annual depreciation of a machine costing ₦500,000 with a useful life of 5 years using the straight-line method.

steps.text: Determine the cost of the asset.
Divide the cost by the useful life.

blocks.markdown: In the reducing-balance method, depreciation is calculated as a fixed percentage of the book value at the beginning of each year. This method is more suitable for assets that lose value quickly.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Always check whether the question specifies a method for calculating depreciation. If not, clarify which method to use.

points: Depreciation spreads the cost of an asset over its useful life.
The straight-line method results in equal depreciation each year.
The reducing-balance method results in decreasing depreciation each year.
